correctness.rationale: For all integer n>=5, double-harmonic unit-sphere vertices have exactly n(n-3)/2 tetrahedral facets made of two disjoint adjacent cyclic pairs; the origin is interior. The oriented cone determinant is D(k)=2 sin^2(h/2)(1-x)(cos h-x)(1+cos h+x), so one-half of the ordered edge pairs divided by 24 yields V=n^2 cos h sin^2 h/48; root-of-unity sums apply for n>=5. With h=2pi/n the limit pi^2/12 and deficit 5pi^4/(18 n^2) follow by Taylor. The seven-angle real circulant Hessian has one rotational zero and three double negative eigenvalues, explicit polynomials in u=cos(2pi/7), hence a strict *local* maximum only modulo rotation. A separate real 4x4 determinant check across n=5,6,7,8,9,12 and finite-difference Hessian spectral check corroborated source algebra; finite samples are not the proof.
